canonicalizer: rfc8785@0.1.4 (Python) / canonicalize@3.0.0 (TypeScript) / gowebpki/jcs v1.0.1 (Go) / cyberphone/json-canonicalization (Java) / serde_jcs@0.2.0 (Rust)

anchored_to.primitive_transition: transition_hash = SHA-256(JCS({action_ref, state, transition_timestamp_ms, authority_verified_at_ms, revocation_check_at_ms}))
load_bearing_invariants: action_ref is byte-stable across every state transition of the same action.
transition_hash is byte-stable for any identical (action_ref, state, transition_timestamp_ms, authority_verified_at_ms, revocation_check_at_ms) tuple.
transition_hash differs per state under identical other-field values.
transition_hash is bound to action_ref: identical state + timestamps under a different action_ref produce a different transition_hash.
action_ref and any transition_hash are byte-distinct.
All timestamp fields are epoch-millisecond integers (Substrate Rule 2); RFC 3339 string forms are rejected at validation time.
anchored_to.spec_authorship: AlgoVoi-authored. The transactional action_ref lifecycle section in x402-foundation/x402 PR #2436 (commit f81f2fe4) is the normative anchor. The transition_hash primitive shape and the five-field preimage discipline are defined in that section.

derivation: Eight vectors split into three groups: (A) a realistic three-state payment lifecycle with distinct transition timestamps per state (vectors 002 to 004); (B) a state-distinctness probe set with identical timestamps under three different states to isolate the state field's byte-load-bearing property (vectors 005 to 007); (C) an action_ref binding vector demonstrating that the same state + timestamps under a different action_ref produces a different transition_hash (vector 008). Vector 001 is the action_ref identity itself (no transition), included so verifiers can reconstruct the action_ref from its four-field preimage independently.

verification_recipe: 1. For each transition vector (002 through 008), take the preimage object verbatim (all five fields).
2. Canonicalise with RFC 8785 (any of the five reference impls in the substrate matrix).
3. base64-encode the JCS bytes; MUST equal expected_jcs_bytes_b64.
4. SHA-256 the JCS bytes, lowercase hex; MUST equal expected_transition_hash.
5. For vector 001 (action_ref identity), the same recipe applied to its four-field preimage MUST yield expected_action_ref.
6. Honour the pair invariants: state-distinctness pairs (005/006, 005/007, 006/007) MUST differ; action_ref-binding pair (005/008) MUST differ; identity-vs-transition pair (001/005) MUST differ.

pair_semantics.state_byte_load_bearing: MUST differ (same action_ref + same timestamps, varying state alone)
pair_semantics.action_ref_binding: MUST differ (same state + same timestamps, varying action_ref)
pair_semantics.identity_vs_transition: MUST differ (action_ref and any transition_hash are byte-distinct under different preimage shapes)

vectors.description: action_ref identity for the fixed preimage. The stable identity anchor across the full lifecycle.
Lifecycle transition: authorisation. First transition of the realistic three-state payment lifecycle, with distinct timestamps per state.
Lifecycle transition: settlement. Second transition of the three-state payment lifecycle.
Lifecycle transition: refund. Third transition of the three-state payment lifecycle.
State-distinctness probe: authorisation under fixed probe timestamps. Isolates the state field to demonstrate it is byte-load-bearing in the preimage.
State-distinctness probe: settlement under the same fixed probe timestamps as 005.
State-distinctness probe: refund under the same fixed probe timestamps as 005 and 006.
Action_ref binding: authorisation under DIFFERENT action_ref but identical state and timestamps to vector 005. Demonstrates that transition_hash is bound to its action_ref.

pair_invariants.description: state byte-load-bearing: authorisation differs from settlement under identical action_ref and identical timestamps
state byte-load-bearing: authorisation differs from refund under identical action_ref and identical timestamps
state byte-load-bearing: settlement differs from refund under identical action_ref and identical timestamps
action_ref binding: identical state and identical timestamps under a different action_ref produce a different transition_hash
identity-vs-transition: the action_ref digest and any transition_hash digest are byte-distinct (different preimage shapes)
